si_thresholds: ST-segment elevation, ST depression, T-wave inversions, or dynamic ECG changes
elevated high-sensitivity troponin in appropriate clinical context
ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation or high-grade AV block (notably with inferior MI)
mechanical complications (VSD, papillary muscle rupture, free wall rupture)
is_requirements: continuous telemetry monitoring for arrhythmia detection
serial cardiac biomarkers for diagnosis and risk stratification
invasive procedures (cardiac catheterization with PCI, or CABG)
intravenous medications (anticoagulation, nitroglycerin, inotropes/vasopressors if shock)
intensive nursing with post-PCI vascular access monitoring
post-procedure arrhythmia, bleeding, and contrast-nephropathy surveillance
two_midnight_expectation: STEMI typically 3-7 days; ACS patients usually cross two midnights. Troponin-negative low-risk chest pain may be an observation candidate; uncomplicated elective PCI may be under two midnights.
denial_downgrade_triggers: troponin-negative chest pain without high-risk features
no documented complications or ongoing ischemia after procedure
overturn_support_factors: documented high-risk features (diabetes, renal insufficiency, multivessel disease, reduced EF, ongoing symptoms)
documented monitoring needs (arrhythmia risk, post-PCI vascular complications)
alignment with specialty guideline recommendations for monitoring duration by cardiac risk
any documented post-procedure complication justifying extended stay

citations.source: Journal of the American College of Cardiology (2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes)
JAMA (Bhatt et al., diagnosis and treatment of acute coronary syndromes: a review)
